title: How He Built a $50,000/Month Vending Business in One Year
excerpt: After a failed restaurant and bankruptcy forced him back into the workforce, he scaled a vending route from 4 machines to 33 in about a year.
quote: Without a doubt, I am so confident that I made the right decision when I joined Vendingpreneurs. As long as I'm in the vending business, I will be part of this community.
body:
## Background

DJ and his wife got into business ownership in 2016. During COVID, a restaurant they owned failed and they went into bankruptcy, forcing both of them back into the workforce in 2021; DJ went into the mortgage industry. He started vending on his own through Naturals2Go, installing his first of four machines in April 2024, before meeting Mike Hoffman at a Wealth Without Wall Street conference in August 2024.

> During COVID, one of the businesses we owned, a little restaurant that just never had a chance to get off the ground, it failed, and we went into bankruptcy as a result of that.

## The Challenge

DJ had already committed to one vending program and had no outside community to validate whether paying for a second one made sense.

> We didn't really look into anything else when we were doing it. Explore different avenues, because you don't know what you don't know, and we really didn't know anything.

## The Turning Point

Seeing Mike Hoffman present at the conference sold him immediately, backed by the appeal of machine flexibility and a community to shorten the learning curve.

> When Mike was up there speaking, I was just like, 'This is my guy right here.' I was so excited. Called my wife, I went up and introduced myself to Mike.

## Where They Are Now

DJ joined in August 2024 with 4 machines and didn't place his fifth until November 2024. By December 2025, he had 33 machines across 17-18 locations, grossing close to $600,000 annualized, or about $50,000 a month. His highest location is student housing at about $8,000 a month; his second-best is a 24/7 warehouse with about 150 employees at around $7,000 a month. He runs three drivers plus a warehouse picker and says vending has replaced at least half of his income from the mortgage business.

> We went from four machines at that time. I'll be installing 32 and 33 next week, so we'll have 33 machines before the end of the year.
review_notes: Location count stated as 'I want to say it's like 17 or 18' - DJ's own estimate, not exact; low end (17) used per range rule.
